subject: Private deploy access patterns: VPC Peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN — recommendation path
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@medicosolutions.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kim@redwood.com>
Cc: NetOps Team <netops@medicosolutions.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy access options — Medico initial ask

Alex / Kim,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we start scoping the Private deployment (VPC + on-prem) for Medico, security and audited access are the primary constraints. Short summary of constraints from our side: HIPAA, explicit egress controls (no broad peering across our VPCs), and infrequent but bursty inference loads (peaks hitting ~6k rps).

We need a short recommendation (1–2 pages) we can hand to procurement and security that explains:
- Which connectivity option (VPC peering, PrivateLink / interface endpoints, or site-to-site VPN) best satisfies strong isolation + predictable latency, and why
- Known operational tradeoffs (routing complexity, NAT/SNAT concerns, cross-account support, multi-region)
- A suggested pilot plan and measurement checklist (latency, failover, throughput, egress cost)

I've attached the requirements doc (medico-privatedeploy-requirements.pdf). Can you both take a pass and propose a recommended path + mutual action plan by Thu 15 Jul? Please call out any blockers for SOC2 / HIPAA review.

Cheers,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Cloud Operations | Medico Solutions
(attachment: medico-privatedeploy-requirements.pdf)

From: alex_martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@medicosolutions.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kim@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy access options — initial recommendation draft

Hi Samira — thanks for the detailed brief and the call. Drafting a concise recommendation below; I'll convert to a 1–2 page PDF and include the measurement checklist (attached: privatelink-vs-peering-checklist.xlsx).

High-level recommendation (short):
- Primary: PrivateLink (AWS Interface Endpoints) from Medico VPCs into Redwood-managed interface endpoints in the same region, with VPC endpoint policies to lock down access. Rationale: strong isolation (no route-table propagation), per-service IAM + endpoint policies, works cross-account without exposing routing plane, and gives us finer control for egress auditing.
- Secondary (fallback): VPC Peering for same-account, low-latency single-region setups where network team requires direct routed connectivity and teams accept routing visibility. Rationale: lowest packet overhead and consistent RTTs, but requires careful CIDR planning and does not support endpoint policies.
- Tertiary (transitional/backup): IPsec site-to-site VPN for on-prem or remote DCs that cannot use PrivateLink. Rationale: universal compatibility, but higher maintenance, less predictable latency, and potential throughput/NAT limits.

Key tradeoffs to call out:
- Security & auditing: PrivateLink gives the clearest boundary for compliance reviewers (no route sharing). Peering requires secure routing controls and additional NAT considerations. VPNs introduce encrypted transit but often lack application-level identity controls.
- Cross-region: PrivateLink is regional (would require multiregion endpoints or fallback). Peering supports inter-region peering (varies by cloud), but operationally we prefer regional collocation for inference latency.
- Performance & scaling: Peering generally lowest RTT; PrivateLink adds an extra network hop and ENI overhead but still within acceptable bounds for lots of customers. VPN throughput and latency will be the weakest for high-volume inference unless using dedicated appliances or AWS Transit Gateway with BW SLAs.

Suggested pilot & measurements (short):
1) Deploy an interface endpoint + endpoint policy in a staging VPC. Run 72-hour synthetic load test (5–6k rps bursts). Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and error rates.
2) Repeat same test over a peering link between a Redwood staging VPC and Medico staging VPC (same AZ if possible). Capture same metrics and compare delta.
3) Run a baseline over a managed IPsec VPN for an on-prem gateway to capture expected latency and jitter.
4) Validate egress billing and NAT behavior: sample tokenized requests and ensure logs show only expected source IPs.

Operational asks / blockers for SOC2 / HIPAA review:
- Provide architecture diagram and flow showing no cross-customer data plane leakage (we'll include in the 1–2 page).
- Endpoint policy templates + least-privilege IAM roles for PrivateLink consumption.
- Proof-of-logs: connection-level flow logs (VPC Flow Logs or equivalent) and request-level audit logs into customer-managed S3 / SIEM.

Next steps: Kim and Marcus, can you add operational caveats (NAT, cross-account role setup) and confirm feasibility of our endpoint setup? I'll produce the deliverable PDF by EOD Wed and we can refine.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
(attachment: privatelink-vs-peering-checklist.xlsx)

From: kimberly_park <kim@redwood.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira@medicosolutions.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy access options — operational caveats

+1 on Alex's structure. A few operational caveats to surface explicitly for Medico's security and netops teams: 

Peering specifics:
- CIDR exhaustion / overlap: Peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs. If Medico's existing VPC addressing overlaps with our staging/test ranges, they'll need readdressing or NAT in front of the peered route.
- No endpoint policies: once peered, routing rules determine reachability; we must enforce access controls at the app layer.

PrivateLink specifics:
- DNAT / ENI counts: Interface endpoints (ENIs) are per AZ and scale; high burst rates can require ENI warm-up; plan for allocation and test for ENI throttling metrics.
- Endpoint policies & IAM: Endpoint policy + resource-based policies on Redwood service must be jointly configured. We'll provide a canonical policy.
- Cross-account role setup: For Medico to invoke endpoints in our account, we need a cross-account consumption model (either roles that assume a mediate role or using endpoint policies referencing their principals). We'll detail the exact policy snippet in the deliverable.

VPN specifics:
- Throughput: Standard cloud-managed IPsec has throughput ceilings; for sustained high bursts use Transit Gateway attachments or customer-managed appliances with higher throughput.
- NAT / MS-MTU & fragmentation: Large token payloads can trigger fragmentation — test with payloads resembling real inference requests (~5–15KB).

Audit & compliance notes:
- Flow logs must be retained for X days as part of HIPAA controls (specify retention per Medico policy). We'll include an S3 lifecycle plan and an example SIEM ingestion pipeline.

I'll add short config snippets and a cutover checklist to the PDF. Marcus: can you run a quick latency sweep between our staging endpoint and the medicos staging VPC (I put a request on NET-125)?

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Network Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: vpn-latency-samples.csv)

From: Samira Khan <samira@medicosolutions.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy access options — agree & ask for a concise memo

Thanks Alex & Kim — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple of follow-ups: 

1) For Procurement: can you add a one-paragraph justification we can paste into our purchase request explaining why PrivateLink is the recommended default and when we'd accept peering or VPN as alternatives?
2) For Security: can you include a short checklist showing which logs/policies we'll need to sign off and who (Redwood vs Medico) will be the owner for each item?

If you can stitch those into the PDF and share by COB today, I'll circulate to our security & procurement leads and confirm a tentative pilot kickoff 26 Jul.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Cloud Operations | Medico Solutions
